description: Captures files stored under a Google Drive folder (including Shared Drives) by recursively walking the folder tree and parsing each downloaded file into records.

scheme.description: auth_type="Service" plus credentials_json: a Google service-account key JSON blob, exchanged for scoped credentials via google.CredentialsFromJSON with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly. The target folder must additionally be shared with the service account's email.

configFields.name: folderUrl
configFields.description: URL of the Google Drive folder to capture from. Must match https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<id>...; the captured id becomes the listing root.

configFields.name: credentials.credentials_json
configFields.description: JSON key of the service account. Required when auth_type=Service.

configFields.name: credentials.client_id
configFields.description: OAuth client id. Required when auth_type=Client.

configFields.name: credentials.client_secret
configFields.description: OAuth client secret. Required when auth_type=Client.

configFields.name: credentials.refresh_token
configFields.description: OAuth refresh token. Required when auth_type=Client.

configFields.name: matchKeys
configFields.description: Regex (format: regex) filter applied to file paths relative to the folder root; non-matching files are skipped.

configFields.name: advanced.ascendingKeys
configFields.description: Declares files are written in ascending lexicographic order so a sweep may resume from the last processed path instead of relisting the whole tree. Default false.

configFields.name: parser
configFields.description: Embedded flow-parser config (format type, compression, csv/json options). Schema is injected at spec time from parser.GetSpec().

configFields.name: stream
configFields.description: Per-binding path prefix to capture; discovery sets it to the Drive folder id extracted from folderUrl.

discovery.method: Drive files.list recursive folder walk (Q: "'<folderId>' in parents"), rooted at the folder id parsed out of folderUrl
discovery.querySketch: files.list(q="'<folderId>' in parents", supportsAllDrives=true, includeItemsFromAllDrives=true, fields="nextPageToken, files(id, name, md5Checksum, mimeType, modifiedTime, size)") paged by nextPageToken
excludes: MIME types beginning with application/vnd.google-apps that are not folders (native Docs/Sheets/Slides) — logged and skipped, never exported
paths outside the shard's key-range hash

backfill.listing: First sweep runs with state MinBound = zero time and MaxBound = now-30s, so every file in the tree whose modifiedTime is below MaxBound is read. Same recursive walk as the incremental leg.

incremental.listing: Depth-first walk of the folder tree held on an in-memory stack. Each folder is enumerated by files.list with q="'<id>' in parents"; readdirAll drains ALL nextPageToken pages for that folder before returning and sorts the entries by file Name. nextPageToken is never checkpointed, so listing NEVER resumes mid-folder — a restart re-lists from the root. Resumption is instead by path: Query.StartAt is set to state.Path (the last path processed) and any entry with StartAt > path that is not a prefix of StartAt is skipped. Folder recursion is transparent (Recursive: true), so IsPrefix entries are never emitted to the sweeper. Each entry carries ObjectInfo.Extra = the Drive file id, which is what Read() uses.

authTierRationale: Two alternative credential modes. The Service Account Key mode is a single self-serve secret blob pasted into one field (plus sharing the folder with the service-account email) — T1_SIMPLE. The Google OAuth mode requires the user to supply client_id, client_secret AND refresh_token in the endpoint config, all three validated as required, which is T3_BYO_REFRESH standalone; the connector does ship a pf.OAuth2 spec (google_auth.Spec) so Estuary's hosted control plane can run the authorization-code dance with its own registered app and mint the refresh token on the user's behalf, but standalone that mode remains T3. authTierOverall takes the easiest offered mode.

unionMisfits.description: The connector encodes no schedule at all. Source.Pull performs exactly one sweep per binding, writes a final checkpoint, and returns; there is no polling loop, sleep, interval or cron anywhere in the connector or in the filesource framework. Cadence is entirely the Flow runtime's decision (it re-opens the Pull RPC). The schema has no way to say 'externally driven, one bounded sweep per invocation'.

proposedShape.unitOfWork: one bounded sweep per Pull RPC
proposedShape.description: connector exits after a single sweep; the platform decides when to invoke it again

unionMisfits.description: The incremental cursor for an object-store connector is a time WINDOW, not a token, and the PullSpec `objects` variant has nowhere to record it. State is {minBound, maxBound, maxMod, path, records, complete}: a sweep fixes maxBound = now + TimeHorizonDelta (-30s) at start, reads only files with minBound < modifiedTime < maxBound, and on completion sets the next minBound = maxMod (the greatest modifiedTime actually processed), not maxBound. With advanced.ascendingKeys=true the semantics change materially — minBound is never advanced and `path` is carried across sweeps instead.

proposedShape.monotonicKeysVariant: ascendingKeys=true freezes minBound and resumes from last path

unionMisfits.description: Objects are downloaded whole (files.get(id).Download(), no byte ranges), but resumption is nonetheless intra-object at RECORD granularity: state.records counts emitted records and state.skip replays-and-discards that many parsed records after a crash. That is neither 'whole-object' nor byte-range chunking.

intraObjectResume.mechanism: checkpointed record count, re-read from byte 0 and discard the first N parsed records

unionMisfits.description: Discovery emits exactly one binding whose resource `stream` is the raw Drive folder id (a user-specific opaque string) while the recommended collection name is the constant "file-data". There is no literal stream list, so the entry above is an archetype named after the recommended collection, not the actual resource path.

proposedShape.cardinality: exactly one binding per configured folderUrl

abstained.streams[0].pull.incremental.format: Set to "auto" because the connector itself never fixes a format: it forwards the user's parser.Config and sets Filename/ContentType from the Drive metadata so flow-parser sniffs. The enumerable format list is owned by github.com/estuary/flow/go/parser (parser.GetSpec()), which is outside this repo and was not read. The extension set in isParquetFile (json, jsonl, csv, tsv, avro, xls, xlsx, xlsm, xml, ods, parquet) is an in-repo mirror of the parser's table and is the best available evidence, but the connector explicitly warns it must be kept in sync, so it may be incomplete.
abstained.streams[0].pull.incremental.compression: Compression is a parser.Config concern (ContentEncoding is forwarded from ObjectInfo, which this store always sets to ""). No compression handling exists in the connector or filesource; the real list lives in the external parser spec.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: No interval, cron, sleep, or ticker exists anywhere in main.go or filesource. Pull performs one sweep and returns, so cadence is set by the Flow runtime, not the connector. Recorded as null rather than guessed.
abstained.streams[0].schedules: Same reason as execution.defaultSchedule — per-binding scheduling is not expressed in the connector.
abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl: objectStore transports have no baseUrl field in this schema; the effective endpoint is the google.golang.org/api/drive/v3 client's default (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3), which is supplied by the vendored SDK rather than by connector code.
abstained.streams[0].writeDisposition: Inferred, not stated. The collection key is (/_meta/file, /_meta/offset), so re-reading a modified file re-emits documents at identical keys and Flow reduces them — effectively merge/upsert. The connector emits no deletes and no tombstones; deleted Drive files simply stop appearing in listings and their prior documents persist. No code names a write disposition.
abstained.streams[0].supportedSyncModes: The resource spec has a SyncMode field but it is jsonschema:"-" (hidden) and never read. Incremental behaviour is implicit in the modtime-window state; there is no user-selectable full_refresh mode. Listed as both because the first sweep is a full sweep, but the connector does not model these as modes.
abstained.execution.continuity.artifacts: Set to null overall: this is a pure read-only poller against Drive (drive.readonly scope). No server-side artifacts are created, no changes-feed startPageToken is requested or stored, nothing accrues on the customer side, and nothing expires on ours — pausing arbitrarily long only means the next sweep sees a wider modifiedTime window.
